results.name: SCKit abuses ScreenConnect to deploy remote access and target technician sessions
results.description: Beginning November 11, 2026, threat actors gained unauthorized access to cloud-hosted ConnectWise ScreenConnect instances belonging to managed service providers. The attackers abuse ScreenConnect, a legitimate remote-support application, to install unauthorized remote-access clients and deploy SCKit, a malicious worm, on customer-managed endpoints. The toolkit establishes persistence through scheduled tasks and registry entries, deploying RelayTrap to deliver malicious payloads to connecting technicians. SCKit targets IT support technician workstations using hijacked authenticated ScreenConnect sessions and uses victim management consoles to distribute payloads to other managed devices. The attack chain includes PowerShell decoders, encrypted bundles using device-specific key material, and browser-access components targeting authenticated ScreenConnect sessions. The worm's deployment enables threat actors to remotely administer affected endpoints, execute commands, and deploy additional tools independently...

results.name: WardenStealer Malware: Turning AI Access into an Underground Commodity
results.description: WardenStealer is a Rust-based Windows infostealer first observed in November 2026 that specializes in stealing credentials, authentication tokens, cookies, API keys, and local AI application files targeting platforms like ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Cursor. Distributed through ClickFix lures, malicious advertisements, cracked software, and fake game cheats, it enables session hijacking that persists even after password resets. The malware operates as malware-as-a-service and captures OAuth tokens, refresh tokens, and configuration data from AI desktop applications. Stolen credentials are monetized in underground markets through discounted subscriptions and API credit reselling, supporting LLMjacking activities. Successful infections expose developer repositories, cloud services, build pipelines, and internal systems, while generating unexpected charges against victim accounts through unauthorized API usage.

results.name: Analysis of NodeLinkRAT, a New North Korea-Linked RAT Abusing Public Note Services as C2
results.description: Between September 12 and 18, 2026, a threat actor impersonating a South Korean National Assembly aide conducted spearphishing attacks against seminar attendees using honorarium payment forms as lures. The attacker deliberately omitted attachments in initial emails to elicit victim replies, then delivered malicious LNK files through webmail. The multistage fileless attack chain involved obfuscated PowerShell scripts, free web hosting, and abuse of aNotepad as a command channel. The actor dynamically changed payloads by updating public note page contents, deploying XenoRAT, information collection scripts, document exfiltration tools, and ultimately NodeLinkRAT—a JavaScript-based remote access tool running on legitimate Node.js runtime. Exfiltration channels rotated among Dropbox, MEGA cloud, and free hosting services. The campaign employed living-off-the-land techniques, polymorphic scripts, and legitimate infrastructure abuse to evade detection while conducting cyberespionage operations targeting South Kore...

results.name: The Retadup USB worm is back to spread CoffeeLoader
results.description: In August 2026, a new CoffeeLoader malware variant was identified, utilizing an NSIS-based installer that drops a patched 7z.dll file containing malicious shellcode. This version employs the Armoury packer, which has been updated to use OpenGL instead of OpenCL for GPU-based decryption. The malware establishes persistence through registry modifications and downloads its main payload from hardcoded C2 servers over HTTPS. The infection vector traces back to the Retadup worm, originally discovered in 2017 and neutralized by French authorities in 2019 after disinfecting 850,000 systems. Since 2024, threat actors have re-registered Retadup's former C2 domains to distribute malware, initially SmokeLoader and later CoffeeLoader, primarily affecting systems in Peru, Angola, Russia, and Bolivia.

results.name: Threat Overview of ARTEX Autonomous Penetration Testing Framework
results.description: ARTEX is an open-source, large language model-driven autonomous penetration testing framework that threat actors have weaponized to automate cyber intrusions from reconnaissance through data exfiltration. Since August 2026, various malicious actors have used ARTEX to conduct global campaigns across multiple sectors, significantly reducing intrusion timeframes with some attacks progressing from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours. Notable incidents include attacks against South Korean financial institutions affecting approximately 67,000 individuals and a supply chain compromise of ConnectWise Cloud Backup impacting over 2,250 downstream customers. Despite the original developer removing the GitHub repository in October 2026, ARTEX continues to proliferate through community forks, archived copies, and a commercial version. results.name: Attackers use Crypto Exchange Names to Disguise Unauthorized Sessions on 100+ ScreenConnect Servers
results.description: Between November 3 and November 13, 2026, threat actors enrolled over 2,200 fake guest sessions across 118 ScreenConnect servers belonging to 109 MSPs and organizations. The unauthorized sessions masquerade as legitimate computers using crypto exchange-themed names like KUCOIN-SRV and BACKUP-PROBIT, displaying screenshots of trading desktops. The majority of connections originated from a single IONOS-hosted IP address. While no malicious activity has been directly observed, investigators suspect these sessions serve as bait to exploit CVE-2026-84869, a critical ScreenConnect vulnerability that could allow malicious guests to execute files on unpatched technician workstations with elevated privileges. The sessions maintain persistent connections every 151 seconds to appear online, potentially waiting for technicians to connect and expose their systems to exploitation.

results.name: GeoVision Camera Software Abused to Deploy XMRig Cryptominer
results.description: Widespread malicious activity was observed targeting GeoVision webcam software between November 8 and November 10, affecting ten accounts and 13 organizations across various industries. Attackers exploited publicly exposed GeoVision devices to execute commands through GeoStartupAgentService.exe under SYSTEM privileges. The attack chain involved PowerShell download cradles retrieving malicious scripts from a remote server, deploying a vulnerable driver for BYOVD attacks, and configuring IFEO Debugger hijacks to disable Windows Defender components. A custom Golang loader utilizing BitTorrent DHT and PKARR resolver was deployed to maintain dynamic command and control infrastructure. The campaign ultimately delivered XMRig cryptominer to hijack computing resources. The incident highlights risks associated with internet-exposed camera management systems and demonstrates sophisticated defense evasion techniques.

results.name: TypoPrompting: From AI Typos to Malware
results.description: Attackers leveraged 186 typosquatting domains across 27 AI brands including Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Perplexity, Midjourney, and ElevenLabs to distribute malicious payloads. Simple typing mistakes lead users to ClickFix lures executing hidden PowerShell commands, Microsoft Store-signed browser-hijacking applications, or search-hijacking extensions. One Claude typo delivered commands from decimal-encoded IP addresses, while others served Net Guard, a Store-signed application containing browser control capabilities. Additional routes deployed search-hijacking extensions affecting 972,000 users. The infrastructure spans 211 entry domains including lookalikes of banks, insurers, and enterprise software, with traffic distribution systems profiling visitors before serving platform-specific lures. This TypoPrompting pattern exploits legitimate workflow interruptions, turning routine AI tool access into malware delivery opportunities through parked domains and sophisticated redirect chains.

results.name: 56 AWS API calls in 141 milliseconds: Inside an AI-run intrusion
results.description: Between September 30 and October 16, 2026, a CyberStrikeAI server executed a sophisticated AWS intrusion spanning four accounts using eight compromised identities. The attack featured machine-speed credential harvesting, with one role executing 56 EC2 user data requests in just 141 milliseconds. The adversary systematically validated stolen credentials, extracted secrets from Secrets Manager, pulled EC2 user data scripts containing sensitive information, and executed remote commands via SSM SendCommand. The attack displayed automated tooling characteristics with intermittent activity across 16 days, including a deliberate 14-day gap that evaded time-based correlation rules. All 78 alerts generated were medium or low severity individually, becoming significant only when correlated by source IP. The intrusion originated from infrastructure in Hong Kong associated with the open-source CyberStrikeAI offensive security platform.

results.name: CVE-2026-88771: Inside the Exploitation of a Critical NetScaler RCE Vulnerability
results.description: On September 27, 2026, Citrix disclosed CVE-2026-88771, a critical remote code execution vulnerability affecting NetScaler Application Delivery Controller and NetScaler Gateway with a CVSS score of 9.8. The vulnerability enables unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands without requiring optional features. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following confirmed worldwide exploitation. Attackers employ a staged exploitation chain involving access-log poisoning, where malicious Base64-encoded payloads are staged in HTTP User-Agent headers, followed by authentication log poisoning using forged PPE failure messages containing shell commands. A vulnerable Perl diagnostic script then executes the poisoned commands with elevated privileges. Observed activities include web shell deployment, PHP enablement, and delivery of FreeBSD implants from infrastructure overlapping with CVE-2026-75650 exploitation targeting Adobe Commerce systems.
